summary: A nine-minute unscheduled call in which the sales manager rings the closer immediately after listening to the end of a call that had just been sold. The prospect — referred to as 'this Thomas guy', the Thomas Proctor call recorded earlier the same day — had verbally agreed, and instead of taking payment on the call Ben sent a payment link and let him go. Chris is blunt that this is a failure, walks Ben through the assumptive onboarding mechanics he wants used instead, and closes with a standing instruction to stop sending payment links. They also touch briefly on a separate prospect, Tristan, who emailed to say he had chosen an in-person trainer, and on note-taking during calls.
notable: STANDING POLICY STATED — 'Well, I called you to say no more sending people payment links and no more letting them get off the call. Just take the sale when it's there.' Management treats a verbal agreement plus a sent payment link as a missed deal, not a close. This directly contradicts the close rule the audit is scoring against, and it means calls dispositioned 'closed' under the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule are internally regarded as unconverted.

The manager frames the outcome as rep-created: 'You didn't give any objection. You created one. You just, you created delay.' Ben agrees, and predicts the consequence himself: 'now you're gonna be chasing this guy down.'

The prescribed close mechanics are assumptive and procedural rather than a question: 'why don't we go ahead and get you started? Onboarding takes, like, two minutes... let me pull this up. What's the best email for you?' and 'what card would you like to put that on?' The manager is explicit about the purpose: 'I get them to just to get them to start moving with me.'
The manager mocks giving the prospect space to reflect, delivered sarcastically as the wrong thing to say: 'Are you sure you don't want to think about it and talk to your spouse before you do this?'

A separate lost deal is reported live and is a clean instance of the known script gap for a cheaper alternative that works: 'This Tristan guy just emailed me back. I've spoken with the person in person, personal trainer, and by comparison, I cannot justify the cost for Trevor's program versus in-person training.' The manager's response — 'we figured that was gonna happen based off the convo' — indicates it was foreseen and not addressed on the call.

The closer repeatedly calls himself a slur on a recorded company call ('I'm retarded', 'I swear I'm not retarded') and refers to a booked prospect as 'this chick'. The manager echoes the first term back once.
Ben reports not taking notes during the sold call and being 'super just locked in'; the manager endorses minimal bullet-point notes over full note-taking.

Title hazard: the file is named only '06/04/2026 - Chris Klevan', the same shape as the prospect-named sales-call titles in this folder. Chris Klevan is the Primal Instinct sales manager, not a prospect.
